articles.title: Paige Bueckers joins rare company as Dallas Wings surge toward playoffs
articles.standfirst: The performance was another example of the all-around excellence that has transformed
articles.summary: The performance was another example of the all-around excellence that has transformed
articles.body:
Paige Bueckers arrived in the WNBA carrying enormous expectations. Less than two full seasons later, she is doing something even more impressive: exceeding them. The Dallas Wings superstar added another chapter to her rapidly growing legacy on Saturday night, leading her team to an 87-82 victory over the Phoenix Mercury while setting a new WNBA scoring milestone that further cemented her place among the league's brightest stars.

Bueckers finished with a game-high 26 points, four rebounds, five assists, three steals, and one block as Dallas secured its sixth consecutive victory. The performance was another example of the all-around excellence that has transformed the former UConn standout from a highly touted prospect into one of the most impactful players in professional basketball.

The win also came on a historic night

During the game, Bueckers became the highest-scoring player through the first two seasons of a WNBA career . The league announced the achievement on social media shortly after the milestone was reached.

“History. Made: Paige Bueckers has scored the most points (1,515) by any player through their first two seasons in WNBA history!”

The record is notable not only because of the names Bueckers passed, but because of what those names represent. She moved ahead of Hall of Famer Seimone Augustus, who scored 1,513 points through her first two seasons, and surpassed WNBA legend Cynthia Cooper, one of the greatest scorers the sport has ever seen.

Bueckers has benefited from the WNBA's expanded 44-game schedule that began during her rookie season in 2025. Augustus established her mark in 68 games, while Cooper accumulated her total in just 58 contests. Even with that caveat, the accomplishment underscores a reality that has become impossible to ignore.

Bueckers is one of the most gifted offensive players in the sport

She reached the milestone in 75 career games and still has two regular-season contests remaining. More importantly, she has paired her scoring ability with elite playmaking, defensive activity, and leadership, turning herself into the centerpiece of a Dallas team that appears to be peaking at exactly the right time. The six-game winning streak is evidence of that growth.

After spending much of the season fighting for playoff positioning, the Wings have surged into the postseason conversation with momentum on their side. Dallas currently sits at 26-16 and occupies sixth place in the standings with road games remaining against Phoenix and Seattle before the playoffs begin. Bueckers has been the driving force behind that rise.

What makes her ascent especially intriguing is the company she is beginning to keep. For much of the past several years, conversations about the league's biggest stars have centered around players such as A'ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, and, more recently, Caitlin Clark. Wilson remains one of the most dominant two-way players in basketball, while Clark has become one of the most influential stars the WNBA has ever seen thanks to her scoring, passing, and ability to transform an offense.

The reigning Rookie of the Year has already become a two-time All-Star and a FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup gold medalist . More importantly, she has demonstrated the ability to impact every facet of the game. On Saturday alone, she scored efficiently, facilitated the offense, generated turnovers, and protected the rim. Few guards in the league offer that complete package.

articles.title: Angel Reese makes history as Wendell Carter Jr. celebrates in style
articles.summary: Angel Reese's record-breaking 2026 season reached another historic milestone Saturday night, and Wendell Carter Jr. was there to celebrate it in style. The Atlanta Dream star became the first player in WNBA history to collect 500 rebounds in a single season during Atlanta's 106-81 victory over the Chicago Sky. Reese finished with 23 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, three blocks and two steals, helping the Dream secure their eighth win in their last 10 games and strengthen their position heading into the postseason. And after the game, Carter once again made sure the spotlight stayed on Reese. The NBA big man, who has become one of Reese's most visible supporters, was spotted rocking another custom Angel Reese jersey following her latest historic performance. It was a fitting celebration for a player who continues to rewrite the WNBA record book in just her third professional season.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and the Fever steal the spotlight before disappointing home game
articles.standfirst: Indiana had a tough afternoon against Washington, although Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull still found a way to turn heads before the game.
articles.summary: Indiana had a tough afternoon against Washington, although Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull still found a way to turn heads before the game.
articles.body:
This Sunday, the Indiana Fever faced the Washington Mystics at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in a game that ended with a 93-77 Washington victory. Caitlin Clark led Indiana in scoring with 25 points, along with 5 assists, 2 rebounds and 2 steals. Kelsey Mitchell added 22 points, while Lexie Hull finished with 2 points and 2 rebounds .

For Sophie Cunningham, the afternoon was even tougher. She came off the bench and played seven minutes without recording any points, rebounds or assists.

So, if there was anything the Fever could brag about that afternoon, it had to happen before the game even started. Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull arrived at the arena in completely different looks and managed to turn some heads before tipoff .

Caitlin Clark went with burgundy

Clark arrived at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in a sporty look centered around burgundy.

The player wore Nike sweatpants with a white T-shirt from the same brand . She added a white-and-burgundy fleece jacket on top, while her sneakers followed the same color combination.

Dark sunglasses, her hair worn down and a few accessories completed the look she chose for her arrival at the game.

Sophie Cunningham completely changed things up

Cunningham showed up in a much more dressed-up combination. The player opted for a dark brown polo shirt with a gray-and-white skirt .

She completed the look with heels, a black handbag, dark sunglasses and a necklace, while leaving her hair down.

The result was quite different from Clark's sporty outfit, showing that there was more than one way to arrive at the same game.

Lexie Hull found the middle ground

Hull arrived in a white blouse and dark brown shorts, paired with a belt in a lighter shade of brown .

Open-toe heels, a handbag and dark sunglasses completed the outfit, while she also wore her hair down.

Her look landed somewhere between the previous two: dressier than Clark's sporty outfit, but not quite as dressed up as Cunningham's.

Now the Fever will have to turn their attention to Minnesota

The loss to Washington is already behind them, and the Fever will not have much time to dwell on it. Indiana will be back in action on Tuesday, September 22, once again at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, this time against the Minnesota Lynx .

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s violent screaming match with Stephanie White caught on camera
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark wasn’t holding back. The Fever star had a heated exchange with coach Stephanie White during a frustrating loss to the Mystics.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark wasn’t holding back. The Fever star had a heated exchange with coach Stephanie White during a frustrating loss to the Mystics.
articles.body:
C aitlin Clar k once again became a topic of conversation after an interaction that may shed light on her relationship with her coach. The Indiana Feve r star shared a tense moment with head coach Stephanie White during the first quarter against the Washington Mystics , at a time when the team was already in trouble.

With Washington leading 31-17 and 58.7 seconds left in the opening period, Clark walked toward the defensive end, turned toward the bench, and expressed her frustration directly at White in full view of everyone .

The exchange stood out because it came just days after the coach had publicly praised her star’s leadership, even saying that Clark “sounds like a coach.”

As the first quarter neared its end, Clark waited for play to resume but used the moment to address White on the sideline. The coach listened while the Indiana point guard made her dissatisfaction clear.

The exchange reflected Clark’s competitive personality. She consistently takes on a leadership role on the court and does not hesitate to speak up when she believes corrections are needed.

The Mystics had taken complete control of the game. Washington closed the first quarter ahead 34-19 and went into halftime with a 51-30 lead .

Kiki Iriafen was key with 21 points and 14 rebounds, while Shakira Austin added 20 points and 10 rebounds in the 93-77 victory.

For Indiana, Clark finished with 25 points and five assists, and Kelsey Mitchell scored 22 points , but the team never mounted a comeback. With two games remaining, Washington moved to within one game of the Fever in the race for the fifth seed.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's frustration: Why the Fever's "lamentable" defensive effort could backfire
articles.standfirst: Indiana's 93-77 loss to Washington exposed defensive problems at the worst possible time, with the Fever now facing the league-leading Minnesota Lynx twice to close the regular season
articles.summary: Indiana's 93-77 loss to Washington exposed defensive problems at the worst possible time, with the Fever now facing the league-leading Minnesota Lynx twice to close the regular season
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever had little time to enjoy their latest winning streak before running into a major warning sign heading into the WNBA playoffs.

After defeating the Toronto Tempo 103-85 on Friday, Indiana returned home Sunday expecting to build more momentum.

Instead, the Fever were overwhelmed by the Washington Mystics , falling 93-77 in a result that left Caitlin Clark visibly frustrated with the team's defensive execution.

Clark still produced 25 points, five assists, two steals and a block, while Kelsey Mitchell contributed 22 points. But Indiana's offense could not compensate for the team's inability to contain Washington , particularly during a disastrous opening stretch.

The Mystics established control almost immediately, opening the game with a 16-8 advantage. Indiana never found a consistent response and eventually fell behind by as many as 26 points.

Washington shot 57% from the field while limiting the Fever to 37%, according to the Associated Press, highlighting the disparity between the two teams on the afternoon.

The problem was not confined to one unit, either. Washington's starters outscored Indiana's starters 74-69, while the Mystics ' reserves also had the upper hand, winning the bench battle 19-8.

For Clark , the most concerning aspect was the way the Fever allowed Washington to gain confidence so quickly.

“I think when you give a team that type of confidence early in the game, you’re just digging yourself a huge hole, and a hole we could never climb out of,” Clark said.

“And, you know, I thought we were just sloppy, sloppy in everything we were trying to execute. I don’t know, our defense was just pitiful and it was frustrating.”

Her comments came after one of Indiana's poorest performances of the season and at a particularly important point in the playoff race.

The Fever entered Sunday sitting fifth in the standings at 27-14 and remained fifth after the defeat, now 27-15. Washington improved to 26-16 and moved within one game of Indiana.

That positioning matters because Indiana is attempting to finish inside the top four, which would provide home-court advantage in the opening playoff round.

The Lynx present an immediate defensive test

Clark was also careful to acknowledge that Washington deserved credit for its performance. She described the Mystics' display as “really beautiful basketball,” but the compliment did not disguise what she believed went wrong for Indiana.

The Fever surrendered 50 points in the paint, an area that Clark specifically highlighted after the game.

“We got to be able to have a coverage in certain things that we can stop them,” Clark added.

That issue could become even more important immediately because Indiana's final two regular-season games are against Minnesota.

The Lynx entered the final stretch of the regular season with the league's best record and moved to 32-10 after defeating Connecticut 101-89 on Sunday. Minnesota also remains in contention for the No. 1 overall seed, making the closing stretch particularly significant.

The Fever and Lynx are scheduled to meet Tuesday, Sept. 22, in Indiana before finishing the regular-season series in Minnesota on Thursday, Sept. 24.

The WNBA's official schedule confirms the back-to-back meetings to close Indiana's regular season.

Indiana already knows how difficult Minnesota can be. The teams met in August, when the Lynx defeated the Fever 108-100 in Minneapolis.

That makes Clark's criticism about the defensive performance particularly relevant. Indiana cannot afford to give another high-level opponent the sort of early confidence Washington found on Sunday, especially against a Minnesota team fighting for the league's top playoff position.

The Fever still have an opportunity to repair the situation before the postseason begins. But the Washington defeat demonstrated how quickly defensive lapses can turn into a runaway deficit.

For a team trying to secure a top-four position, the final two games therefore represent more than routine regular-season contests. They will give Indiana a chance to test whether the problems Clark identified can be corrected before the games become even more consequential.

And with the Lynx waiting, the Fever will not have to wait long to find out.

articles.title: Where to watch Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty? TV channel and game time for Angel Reese’s team
articles.standfirst: Atlanta Dream bring East's best record to Barclays for Liberty Clash
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream bring East's best record to Barclays for Liberty Clash
articles.body:
The last games of the regular season arrive at Barclays Center on Monday night as the New York Liberty host the Atlanta Dream, a matchup between two of the Eastern Conference's heavyweights that promises to set the tone for the WNBA Playoffs.

This is a collision of experience and momentum — a Liberty side chasing another deep run against an Atlanta team that finished the regular season as the top club in the East.

When and where to watch the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty?

Tip-off is scheduled for the early hours of Monday, 21 September 2026 at 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time (7:00 p.m. Central Time and 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time). The game is staged at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, a venue with a capacity of 18,732.

American audiences can find WNBA coverage across different TV channels and streaming services; however for this game between Atlanta and New York, you’ll be able to watch it on NBCSN and Peacock.

Two contenders, separated by fine margins

The regular-season table tells a story of near-equals. Atlanta tops the Eastern Conference with a 28–14 record, edging out a crowded pack behind them. New York is currently third in the East at 26–16, a game and a half back but every bit as dangerous.

Looking at the wider league picture and the two sides are practically inseparable: Atlanta sits fourth overall and New York seventh, but both carried 24 points in the combined standings, underlining just how tight this bracket has become.

The numbers reinforce that. Atlanta was one of the most productive offensive teams in the conference, pouring in 3,841 points across the season while conceding 3,568 — a points differential of +273 that ranked among the best in the East.

New York's profile is more measured: 3,792 scored against 3,624 allowed for a +168 differential. The Dream have the sharper margin, but the Liberty's championship-tested core means these season totals only tell part of the tale.

New York Liberty: star power and continuity

The Liberty roster remains stacked with elite talent. Sabrina Ionescu runs the show from the backcourt, flanked by the versatility of Breanna Stewart and Satou Sabally up front, with Jonquel Jones anchoring the interior.

That quartet gives head-office belief that New York can trade blows with anyone in a seven-game or single-elimination format. Germany's Leonie Fiebich adds two-way length on the wing, while the backcourt has a distinct international flavour with France's Marine Johannes, Marine Fauthoux and Pauline Astier all on the books.

The frontcourt depth is a genuine asset. Alongside Jones, New York can lean on the size of Han Xu and Spain's Raquel Carrera, and the athleticism of Rebecca Allen and Australia's Anneli Maley on the wing. With home-court advantage in Brooklyn and a raucous Barclays crowd behind them, the Liberty will want to impose their pace and physicality from the opening whistle.

Atlanta Dream: the East's form team

Atlanta earned their conference crown on the strength of a balanced, deep group. Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard form one of the most dynamic scoring backcourts in the league, capable of taking over stretches on their own. Veteran DeWanna Bonner brings postseason scars and steadiness, while Jordin Canada offers speed and disruption at the point of attack.

The Dream frontcourt is where much of the intrigue lies. Angel Reese has become a magnet for attention on the glass and around the rim, and she is paired with the interior toughness of Brionna Jones and the energy of Naz Hillmon.

Mali's Sika Kone and Kenya's Madina Okot add further length inside, giving Atlanta a rotation that can go big or spread the floor with shooters like Te-Hina Paopao. The rebounding battle between Reese, Brionna Jones and New York's Jonquel Jones could well decide possessions in a game this closely matched.

Players to watch during the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty game

Sabrina Ionescu (New York): The engine of the Liberty offence, equally capable of orchestrating for others or shouldering the scoring load when the game tightens. In a series this fine, her decision-making down the stretch could be the difference.

Allisha Gray (Atlanta): The Dream's leading scoring threat and a two-way handful, Gray sets the tone for Atlanta's transition game and will be central to any road success at Barclays.

Angel Reese (Atlanta): Her work on the offensive glass creates second-chance points that can quietly swing tight postseason games. If she wins her battle inside, Atlanta's ceiling rises considerably.

Prediction for the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty game

This has the makings of a coin-flip. Atlanta arrive with the better regular-season record and the sharper points differential, but New York's home floor, championship experience and elite top-end talent are difficult to bet against in a Barclays Center opener. Expect a physical, high-possession contest decided in the final minutes — and a narrow New York win to set an early tone in the game.

Mali's Sika Kone and Kenya's Madina Okot add further length inside, giving Atlanta a rotation that can go big or spread the floor with shooters like Te-Hina Paopao. The rebounding battle between Reese, Brionna Jones and New York's Jonquel Jones could well decide possessions in a game this closely matched.
Players to watch during the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty game

Sabrina Ionescu (New York): The engine of the Liberty offence, equally capable of orchestrating for others or shouldering the scoring load when the game tightens. In a series this fine, her decision-making down the stretch could be the difference.
Allisha Gray (Atlanta): The Dream's leading scoring threat and a two-way handful, Gray sets the tone for Atlanta's transition game and will be central to any road success at Barclays.
Angel Reese (Atlanta): Her work on the offensive glass creates second-chance points that can quietly swing tight postseason games. If she wins her battle inside, Atlanta's ceiling rises considerably.
Prediction for the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty game

This has the makings of a coin-flip. Atlanta arrive with the better regular-season record and the sharper points differential, but New York's home floor, championship experience and elite top-end talent are difficult to bet against in a Barclays Center opener. Expect a physical, high-possession contest decided in the final minutes — and a narrow New York win to set an early tone in the game.

articles.title: Where to watch Dallas Wings vs Phoenix Mercury? TV channel and game time for the Paige Bueckers game
articles.standfirst: Kelsey Plum's Mercury Host Paige Bueckers and the Wings
articles.summary: Kelsey Plum's Mercury Host Paige Bueckers and the Wings
articles.body:
The 2026 regular season told contrasting stories for these clubs and this Monday night, Paige Bueckers’ Dallas Wings play one of their last games of the 2026 regular season at against the Pheonix Mercury.

The Dallas Wings finished at 26-16, landing fourth in the Western Conference and holding a healthy scoring margin — 3,744 points scored against 3,573 conceded, a plus-171 differential across 42 games. That balance of offense and defense marks them as a genuine threat.

Phoenix, by contrast, backed into this matchup the hard way. The Mercury closed the year 15-27, seventh in the West, and were outscored on the season (3,543 for, 3,668 against, a minus-125 differential).

On paper, Dallas arrives as the favorite. But the Footprint Centre can be a difficult place to play, and Phoenix has the individual talent to swing any single night.

Where to watch the Dallas vs Phoenix game and what time is staring

The Phoenix Mercury are playing their last regular season game at home against the Dallas Wings this Monday, September 22, tipping off at 10:00 p.m. Eastern Time (9:00 p.m. Central Time and 7:00 p.m. Pacific Time) at the Footprint Centre in Phoenix.

It's a matchup that pits backcourt star power against playoff experience, and both rosters are stacked with names capable of taking over a game.

American viewers can catch the action across the WNBA's including the Dallas vs Pheonix game at USA Network and streaming with the WNBA League Pass.

Dallas Wings vs Phoenix Mercury Rosters and players to watch: Star Power on Both Sides

This game is loaded with recognizable names. For Phoenix, guard Kelsey Plum headlines a backcourt that also features veteran Sami Whitcomb. The Mercury's frontcourt carries serious pedigree in Alyssa Thomas, one of the league's most versatile forwards, alongside scoring wing Kahleah Copper. That trio gives Phoenix the kind of two-way firepower that can neutralize a talent gap over 40 minutes of basketball.

Dallas counters with a young, dynamic guard rotation. Paige Bueckers, at 24, leads the way alongside sharpshooter Azzi Fudd and dangerous scorer Arike Ogunbowale, whose ability to erupt from the perimeter can flip a game in a matter of possessions. Up front, Alanna Smith and Jessica Shepard provide size and rebounding, while veteran Alysha Clark brings championship-tested composure to the wing.

The clash of styles is fascinating: Dallas leans on youthful pace and outside shooting, while Phoenix relies on the physicality and playoff nous of Thomas, Copper, and Plum.

The single most compelling subplot is the guard duel. Bueckers and Fudd represent the Wings' present and future, a pairing built for tempo and three-point volume. Phoenix will lean on Plum to answer shot-for-shot — she's the kind of scorer who thrives on the postseason stage, and the burden of keeping the Mercury afloat offensively will fall largely on her shoulders.

If Ogunbowale gets hot from deep, Dallas becomes very hard to stop. Conversely, if Thomas can dominate the glass and control the pace, she can drag Phoenix into the kind of half-court grind that suits the Mercury far more than the Wings.

Paige Bueckers (Dallas): The 24-year-old guard is the engine of the Wings' attack. How she handles the pressure of the moment against a veteran Phoenix defense could define the series.

Kelsey Plum (Phoenix): The Mercury's go-to scorer. If Phoenix is going to pull the upset, Plum almost certainly has to deliver a big night.

Alyssa Thomas (Phoenix): A do-everything forward whose rebounding, passing, and defense can tilt the tempo. When Thomas is engaged, Phoenix plays a level up.

Arike Ogunbowale (Dallas): A volume scorer capable of a single-handed run that puts a game out of reach.

Prediction for the Dallas Wings vs Phoenix Mercury

The numbers favor Dallas. The Wings are currently with a far superior record and a positive scoring margin, while Phoenix limped to the finish line and was outscored on the year.

Expect the Wings' young backcourt to test a Mercury defense that leaked points all season. That said, Phoenix has the star quality — Plum, Thomas, and Copper — to make this a genuine fight, and home court at a packed Footprint Centre is worth something.

The lean here is Dallas to take the opener, but don't be surprised if Phoenix's veterans keep it close deep into the fourth quarter. A high-scoring, guard-driven affair looks likely — one where the last few possessions decide it.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark watches Sophie Cunningham’s role shrink as the Fever prepare for the WNBA playoffs
articles.standfirst: The Fever suffered their first double-digit loss since July in their last game against Washington
articles.summary: The Fever suffered their first double-digit loss since July in their last game against Washington
articles.body:
The 30th WNBA regular season is coming to an end this week with Thursday being the last day of action before the playoffs begin on September 27th with the first round being a best-of-three series.

Although the eight playoff-bound teams ( Lynx , Valkyries , Aces , Dream , Fever , Liberty , Wings , Mystics ) have been locked in for weeks, exact seeding remains undecided with only two games left, featuring a tight race for positions six through eight and the second-place Valkyries hunting down Minnesota at the top of the table.

For the league's most popular franchise, the Indiana Fever, the final stretch is intensely demanding with their last two matchups pitting them against the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx both at home and on the road.

Right now, the Fever sit in fifth place in the overall standings, but can finish as low as the eighth seed or as high as third depending on this week's results.

Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull See Playing Time Dip

In the Fever's last outing , the team stumbled in a 93-77 defeat to the Washington Mystics, marking their first double-digit loss since July 15 and the first time they scored fewer than 80 points since that same mid-July stumble against the Valkyries.

The tactical adjustments led to notable shifts in playing time, with sharpshooters Lexie Hull and Sophie Cunningham seeing their roles shrink significantly. Hull struggled to find a rhythm and was benched at halftime in favor of rookie Raven Johnson , finishing with just 13 minutes of action.

Meanwhile, Cunningham, typically Indiana's primary sparkplug off the bench, logged a mere 7 minutes on the floor and went 0-for-2 from the field , failing to record a point, rebound, or assist.

Speaking to reporters after the game, coach White addressed what she needs from the supporting cast moving forward: "We've got to get them the ball in positions to get good shots, and make shots. And they've got to help us on the defensive end and rebounding the basketball."

Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell Lead Record-Breaking Offense

Even with the setback, Indiana boasts the most explosive offense in league history , averaging 96.7 points per game with a record 20 games scoring over 100 points .

Spearheaded by Kelsey Mitchell (averaging 25.1 points per game , second-best in the WNBA) and maestro Caitlin Clark , who is orchestrating the most offensively productive season in league history as the third-best scorer ( 22.7 PPG ) and assist leader ( 8.4 APG ), the superstar backcourt combined for another milestone.

During the loss, both players crossed the 20-point threshold , extending their shared WNBA single-season record to 21 games with 20+ points each.

However, a brutal defensive start and early offensive stagnation, compounded by foul trouble for Aliyah Boston , exposed vulnerabilities against a tough Mystics frontline, prompting head coach Stephanie White to aggressively adjust her rotations.

As the postseason approaches, tightening rotations is expected, but the recent struggles underscore a glaring reality: the Fever remain heavily reliant on their elite trio of Clark, Mitchell, and Boston , all of whom are premier All-Star talents ranked among the league's top-tier performers.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark rapping during a Fever timeout might just be worthy of a Grammy
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark found another way to entertain the crowd during an Indiana Fever timeout.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark found another way to entertain the crowd during an Indiana Fever timeout.

As music played inside the arena, the Fever superstar was caught enthusiastically rapping along from the bench. Clark appeared to know every word, delivering the lyrics with enough confidence and energy to turn the timeout into her own personal performance.

The hilarious moment quickly spread across social media, where fans joked about Clark potentially adding a music career to her already impressive résumé. Basketball remains her greatest talent, but after this performance, a future Grammy appearance might not be completely out of the question.

articles.title: WNBA History: Caitlin Clark silences critics with a legendary scoring milestone
articles.standfirst: The Fever star became the highest-scoring point guard in a single season
articles.summary: The Fever star became the highest-scoring point guard in a single season
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark didn't need long to remind the WNBA that one broken rookie record does not diminish the scale of what she is building in Indiana.

Olivia Miles had just moved past Clark ’s rookie scoring total with another standout performance for the Minnesota Lynx .

Only hours later, Clark produced a milestone of her own, reaching 862 points this season and setting a new single-season scoring record for a WNBA point guard.

Clark got there after scoring 25 points against the Washington Mystics , continuing a remarkable third professional season in which she has averaged 22.7 points per game while shooting 45.1 percent from the field.

The record also highlights just how much more efficient Clark has become since her rookie campaign. She reached 862 points in 38 games. Her previous rookie total of 769 came across 40 appearances.

Miles takes one of Clark’s rookie records

The timing made the achievement even more striking. Earlier in the day, Miles entered Minnesota’s game against the Connecticut Sun tied with Clark ’s rookie scoring mark of 769 points.

She moved ahead with a second-quarter free throw and finished with 21 points in the Lynx ’s 101-89 victory, lifting her season total to 790.

“It’s special, but it means we’re more so working well as a team,” Miles said afterward. “I have great teammates around me, great vets who allow me to be me out there.”

Miles also pointed to Minnesota’s support system as a major factor in her rapid rise.

“It wouldn’t be possible without one, a coach that believes in you and then two, having teammates that have my back,” she said. “So it’s really special to obviously be able to accomplish that with such a great team and on a win as well.”

Miles has taken more than one rookie mark from Clark this season. She hit eight three-pointers against the Golden State Valkyries in June, surpassing Clark ’s rookie single-game record of seven, and became the fastest rookie to reach 350 points, 100 rebounds and 100 assists.

Clark’s latest record moves conversation

Clark ’s response came in a different category entirely. Her 862 points represent the most ever by a point guard in a single WNBA season, moving her beyond comparisons with her own rookie year and into the league’s broader record book.

That gives the final two regular-season meetings between Indiana and Minnesota an added layer of intrigue. Clark and Miles are scheduled to meet in Indiana on September 22 before the teams close the season in Minneapolis two days later.

Minnesota is fighting to secure the No.1 seed, while Indiana is still trying to strengthen its playoff position. The individual storyline will be difficult to ignore.

Miles has already erased several of Clark ’s rookie records. Clark , meanwhile, is now setting marks that apply to every point guard who has played in the league.
